new_statements.translation: b. Nothing about the accent has come down to us from the period of our monuments, but certain indications suggest that in early times the stem carried a stronger stress than the formatives; the initial stress thus to be presupposed probably also explains the East Turkic poets' preference for the trochaic ramal metre and their inclination to alliteration (see § 188e). c. The initial stress also explains the widespread tendency to suppress the second syllable of a word before an affix, or, in monosyllabic words, the first syllable of an affix, when it contains palatal or velar i or u.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The source states that word accent is not attested for the written Islamic East Turkic languages (Karakhanid through Chagatai): no synchronic stress rule can be given. It infers only that at an earlier stage the stem (initial) syllable bore stronger stress than suffixes, using this to explain syncope of high vowels in post-initial syllables and the poets' metrical/alliterative habits; elsewhere in the same section it notes that in derivatives like *tisiq- > ciq- the stress passed from the stem to the derivational syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: The reconstructed stem stress is said to have shifted to the derivational syllable in some derivatives (*tisiq- > ciq- 'herauskommen', par. 161a, 'der Druck vom Stamm auf die Ableitungssilbe uebergegangen', with reference to Benloew's 'principe du dernier determinant').
new_statements.domain_note: Written literary language known only from Arabic-script manuscripts; the statement is about the whole corpus of the Islamic Central Asian Turkic literary languages ('unsrer Denkmaeler'), the syncope examples are from Kasgari (11th c. Karakhanid), and the metrical argument concerns East Turkic poetry. No distinction of word vs phrase level, no citation forms.
new_statements.identity_note: Chagatai is an extinct Arabic-script literary language (15th-early 20th c. Central Asia; ISO chg). The only statement found, Brockelmann 1954 par. 10 b-c, is about the Islamic Central Asian Turkic literary languages jointly (Karakhanid of Kasgari/Qutadgu Bilig, Khwarezmian, and Chagatay of Nava'i etc.) and explicitly says accent is unattested 'aus der Zeit unsrer Denkmaeler'; its syncope examples are Karakhanid (11th c.), not Chagatai. Blagova 1997 nevertheless lists Brockelmann 1954 in the Chagatai bibliography. The Jazyki mira sketch (Blagova 1997), the only full description held by the project, is for the classical literary language and is silent on stress.
